To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) FCDD is a novel deep one-class classification architecture that provides explanations for anomaly detection; (b) FCDD sets a strong new state of the-art on the MVTec-Ad benchmark; (c) using even a few ground-truth anomaly masks improves FCDD's performance; (d) FCDD is vulnerable to spurious image artifacts, such as watermarks.

FCDD is an explainable, competitive deep one-class classification model for anomaly detection; FCDD can be trained with ground-truth anomaly masks and does so effectively; and, using FCDD explanations, we demonstrate that deep one-class models can be misled by spurious features.

(i) we present an explainability method for deep one-class classification that yields state-of-the-art anomaly detection performance on the MVTec-Ad dataset, and (ii) we find that deep one-class models are susceptible to spurious image artifacts such as watermarks, and (iii) that our method can be used to detect such artifacts.
